model.covariance: rho_ij * overlap/H; rho_ij=1 same title else mean pairwise daily-return correlation
limitations: Equal variances and no serial correlation assumed
Correlation estimated on the last ~6 months only; regime dependent
Sector/size clustering beyond the mean correlation ignored (understates dependence)
Yardstick for design, not an inferential result

findings: Observed: 4137 events on 20 dates / 6 ISO weeks / 2 months; all M6 windows overlap (1 non-overlapping M6 block).
Mean pairwise daily-return correlation 0.061 raw, 0.079 SPY-excess.
N_eff for the mean M6 outcome of all events: raw 17.1, SPY-excess 13.3 (n=4137).

20 consecutive weeks x 200 titles (n=4000) give raw N_eff 22.0: twenty calendar weeks are not twenty independent observations of an M6 outcome; overlapping horizons and the common market factor dominate.

Neither a month count nor an ISO-week count measures independence. A dependence-aware criterion (minimum N_eff from a declared cluster/block model, plus a minimum number of non-overlapping horizon blocks) is required to make the gate meaningful.

proposal: Keep the active gate (calendar months, independentWeeks=20) unchanged until owner approval.

If changed: rename the field to what is counted (eventCalendarWeeks) and add a separate independence gate: minimum effective sample size of the M6 endpoint under a pre-registered calendar-block/cluster model (e.g. N_eff >= 30 on SPY-excess returns) AND at least k non-overlapping M6 horizon blocks (e.g. k >= 4, i.e. >= ~2 years of history).
Report raw and market-excess N_eff on every certification build; never infer independence from event counts.
recommendationUpdate.consequence: A real independence requirement for M6 outcomes is materially stricter than either counter: with ~1 non-overlapping M6 block today, setup certification cannot be justified on independence grounds before multiple years of forward-collected history.
